summary: Sokichi Tsuda (1873–1961) specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō (~1890–1891), worked at the SMR Research Department (~1908–1918), and held posts at Waseda University (~1918–1940) and the University of Tokyo (~1939–1940).

Soko Morinaga (1925–1995) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Toyama High School, Daitoku-ji, and under Sesso Oda and Zuigan Goto. He later served as abbot at Daishuin (~1963–1995) and head of Hanazono University (1986–1994).

Sokuo Eto (1888–1958) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. He later served as head of Komazawa Junior College (~1950–1958) and as a professor at Komazawa University in 1953.

Solomon George FitzHerbert works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford, where he served as Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies, and held a research post at the CNRS (attested 2019).

Soma Thera (1898–1960) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, and trained under Jetavana Sayadaw in 1936. Between ~1929 and 1936, he was a member of Servants of the Buddha.

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Oxford, the French Institute of Pondicherry, Kyoto University, and Columbia University as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit.

Somboon Watana works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Panjab University in 1999 under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma, and became an assistant professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

Somchai Kusalacitto specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara (1913–2013) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Vajirayanavangsa, Swami Satyananda Puri, and at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara, where he served as abbot (~1961–2013). He also directed Mahamakut Buddhist University in 1961.

Somphong Santacitto is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

Sonam Chhoki is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. at SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Choden specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She worked as a doctoral local researcher and as a project staff member (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin) at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Sonam Gyatso (b. 1933) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko around 1961 and served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).
Sonam Jamtsho specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with the University of Hamburg as a doctoral local researcher and scientific project staff member (attested 2026).

Sonam Kachru works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold and has held posts at the Max Planck Institute, Forum Transregionale Studien, and Yale University (attested 2026).

Sonam Kinga (b. 1973) is a historian and Tibetologist. He studied at Sherubtse College (~1994–1998) and Kyoto University (~2003–2006), and served as a researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (~1999–2007).

Sonam Thakchoe specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1998–2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, and held a post at the University of Tasmania around 2003.

Sonam Tsering specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Gray Tuttle and serves at Columbia University as Senior Lecturer in Tibetan and Director of the Tibetan Language Program (attested 2026).
Sondra L. Hausner works in religious studies and Indology. She serves as Professor of Anthropology of Religion at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).
Songeun Choe works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).
